## Purpose

This SOP describes field procedures for collecting, filtering, and
preserving environmental DNA (eDNA) samples from surface waters. eDNA
consists of DNA shed into the environment by organisms through skin
cells, mucus, feces, gametes, and decomposing tissue. Detecting eDNA
in water samples allows non-invasive detection of aquatic species
(fish, amphibians, invertebrates, pathogens) without direct
observation or capture [@goldberg2016]. Because eDNA is present at
extremely low concentrations, preventing contamination during field
collection is critical. This SOP covers the field side of the
workflow; laboratory processing (filtration, extraction, inhibition
testing) is covered in
[SOP-L700 DNA Extraction](../lab_sops/SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Collection and preservation of water samples for
  eDNA analysis at all EA Program surface water sites (streams, lakes,
  ponds, wetlands, stormwater basins)
- **Does not apply to:** Soil eDNA or soil microbial sampling (see
  [SOP-F701](SOP-F701-soil-microbial-field-sampling.qmd)); tissue
  biopsy or organism capture for DNA; airborne eDNA sampling;
  lab-side filtration, extraction, and molecular analysis
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve sampling design; ensure permits are in place    |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and preserve eDNA samples per this SOP          |
| New Students      | Complete training (including contamination awareness)
                      before participating in eDNA sampling                |


## Definitions

- **Contamination (eDNA):** The introduction of exogenous DNA from
  sources other than the target organism into a sample or filter;
  the single largest source of false positives in eDNA surveys;
  prevented by sterile technique, glove changes between samples, and
  decontamination of reusable equipment [@goldberg2016].
- **eDNA (environmental DNA):** Genetic material shed into the
  environment by organisms through mucus, feces, gametes, skin cells,
  and other biological material; collected from water without direct
  capture of the target organism; detectable at extremely low
  concentrations using PCR-based methods [@goldberg2016].
- **Equipment blank:** A control sample consisting of deionized water
  rinsed through decontaminated reusable equipment (e.g., a pump)
  and collected as a sample; detects carry-over contamination between
  sites when dedicated equipment is not used.
- **Field blank:** A sterile bottle of molecular-grade deionized water
  opened and handled at the field site under identical conditions to
  real samples; filtered and preserved like a field sample; detects
  airborne or handling contamination during field work; must yield no
  target amplification [@goldberg2016].
- **Filter pore size:** The nominal diameter of pores in the filter
  membrane; 0.45 µm is the standard for eDNA capture from surface
  water, retaining bacteria, cells, and particulate-bound DNA.
- **Longmire's buffer:** A non-freezing preservation solution
  (containing EDTA, Tris, NaCl, SDS, and sucrose) used to preserve
  eDNA on filters in the field when immediate freezing is not possible;
  inactivates nucleases and inhibits microbial degradation
  [@renshaw2015].
- **Open-channel filtration:** A filtration method using a funnel and
  vacuum pump or syringe; the filter membrane is exposed to the
  environment during collection, increasing contamination risk
  compared to closed-capsule methods.
- **PCR inhibitor:** A substance co-extracted with eDNA that suppresses
  PCR amplification efficiency; common in natural water samples
  (humic acids, tannins, metal ions); detected by running a dilution
  series of the extract and checking for concentration-dependent
  amplification; managed by diluting the extract or using commercial
  inhibitor removal kits.
- **Sterivex filter:** A commercially available enclosed 0.22 µm
  polysulfone cartridge filter; preferred for eDNA because the sealed
  design minimizes contamination, allows direct addition of
  preservation buffer, and is compatible with standard extraction kits
  [@renshaw2015].
- **Target species detection:** The determination of presence or absence
  of a specific taxon in a water sample based on amplification of
  taxon-specific eDNA; sensitivity depends on eDNA shedding rate,
  water volume filtered, PCR method, and inhibitor load in the extract
  [@goldberg2016].
- **Volume filtered:** The total volume of water passed through a
  filter during sample collection; a required reporting variable for
  calculating eDNA concentration; record for every filter regardless
  of whether filtration was complete or the filter clogged
  [@goldberg2016].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Wading and sampling near water carry slip, fall, and
  drowning hazards. Work in pairs.
- **Chemical:** DNA preservatives (ethanol, Longmire's buffer) are
  flammable (ethanol) or contain EDTA and SDS (Longmire's). Handle
  with gloves.
- **Biological:** Water may contain pathogens. Wear gloves and avoid
  ingestion.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (change between every sample)
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Wading boots or waders (if entering the water)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Sampling Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Sterile 1 L HDPE sample bottles       | One per sample; single-use               |
| 60 mL sterile syringes                | For Sterivex filtration                  |
| Sterivex 0.22 µm filter capsules      | Preferred; one per sample                |
| 0.45 µm PES open filter funnels       | Alternative to Sterivex                  |
| Longmire's buffer (1--2 mL per filter) | For filter preservation without freezing [@renshaw2015] |
| Molecular-grade ethanol (95%)         | Alternative preservative for Sterivex    |
| Molecular-grade deionized water       | For field blanks (1 bottle per event)    |
| Cooler with ice packs (4 °C)          | For sample transport if not filtering on-site |


## Procedure

### Pre-Field Preparation

1. Prepare all equipment in the lab using UV-decontaminated surfaces
   and dedicated pre-PCR equipment.
2. Pre-label all bottles and filters with project ID, site, replicate
   number, date.
3. Pack a cooler with ice packs or dry ice.
4. Include at least one sterile bottle of molecular-grade DI water
   per sampling event for field blanks.

### Water Collection

1. Put on fresh nitrile gloves.
2. Open the sterile bottle only when ready to collect.
3. Submerge the bottle to 10--20 cm below the water surface, facing
   upstream, away from your body [@goldberg2016].
4. Fill to 1 L and cap immediately.
5. For composite samples: collect 250 mL from each of 4 microhabitats
   and combine in one bottle.
6. Record the GPS coordinates, collection time, and site conditions.

### Field Filtration (If Filtering On-Site)

**Sterivex capsule method:**

1. Attach a sterile 60 mL syringe to the Sterivex filter inlet.
2. Draw water from the sample bottle and push through the filter.
   Repeat until the filter clogs or 1 L has been filtered. Record
   the total volume filtered.
3. Expel remaining water from the capsule.
4. Add 1--2 mL of Longmire's buffer or fill with molecular-grade
   ethanol using a syringe [@renshaw2015]. Cap both ends of the
   Sterivex.
5. Label the capsule and place in a ziplock bag on ice.

**Open filter funnel method:**

1. Pour the sample through a sterile 0.45 µm PES filter unit.
2. Use sterile forceps to fold the filter membrane in half (sample
   side inward) and place in a labeled cryovial.
3. Add preservative (ethanol or Longmire's buffer) to cover the
   filter. Seal.
4. Place on ice immediately.

### If Not Filtering On-Site

Keep whole-water samples on ice (4 °C) and filter in the lab within
6 hours of collection. Exceeding 6 hours significantly increases DNA
degradation [@goldberg2016].

### Field Blanks and Controls

- **Field blank:** Open the sterile DI water bottle at one site per
  event, filter it using the same method as field samples, and
  preserve. This blank detects contamination during field handling.
- **Equipment blank:** If any reusable equipment contacts the sample,
  collect a deionized water rinse blank after decontamination.
- Process blanks through the entire lab workflow alongside samples.

### Decontamination Between Sites

1. Spray or soak all reusable equipment with 10% bleach solution for
   at least 1 minute.
2. Rinse with clean water.
3. Change gloves.
4. Single-use items (bottles, filters, syringes) are discarded after
   each sample.

See [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd) for general
decontamination procedures.


## Sample Transport and Storage

1. Keep all samples and preserved filters on ice (4 °C) during
   transport.
2. Deliver to the lab the same day. If overnight storage is
   unavoidable, store at -20 °C.
3. For long-term storage (> 1 week before extraction), store preserved
   filters at -20 °C or -80 °C.
4. Complete the chain of custody form per
   [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd).


## Quality Control

- Minimum 1 field blank per sampling event; 1 equipment blank if
  reusable equipment is used.
- Collect 3 replicate samples per site unless the study design
  specifies otherwise.
- Record the total volume filtered for each sample.
- Any field blank positive for target DNA invalidates samples from
  that event unless below a pre-established threshold. Consult the PI.
- Log all glove changes, bottle openings, and deviations in the field
  notebook.

## Training Record

Before collecting eDNA samples independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd), and
   [SOP-L700](../lab_sops/SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate proper sterile technique (glove changes, bottle
   handling, filter preservation) during a supervised practice session
3. Successfully process a field blank with a negative result
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
